deep.reconstruction:
The page contains no mathematics. It has two non-mathematical blocks.

(1) Lists of numbers headed by dates and letters. '1830. Mai 1': series A: 166, 376, 459; B: 159, 193, 360, 364; C: 28, 57, 141, 418, 518; G: 136, 290, 331, 385, 927, 1045, 1095, 1614, 2018, 2462, 2669, 2675, 2782, 3234, 3336, 3538, 3825, 4012, 4042, 4062, 4191, 4220, 4560; K: 1294. 'Jun. 1': A: 203, 325; K: 33, 173, 414, 473, 738; G: 383, 480, 1141, 1311, 1339, 1898, 2878, 3076, 4607. Then 'ohne litera 1803. Sept. 1. Nro 29' ('without a letter, issue of 1 Sept 1803, no. 29'). The format (letter series, serial numbers, drawing dates of 1 May and 1 June, an unlettered item identified by issue date) suggests these are serial numbers of state bonds or obligations called in a periodic drawing (Verlosung/Auslosung). Gauss may have been checking his own holdings or those he managed. This reading is inferred from the format, not stated on the page. No calculation is performed.

(2) Notes on inheritance law. The quotation is the reference 'l. 3 C. de lib. praet.', i.e. Codex Iustinianus 6.28.3 (title 'de liberis praeteritis vel exheredatis'). It reads: 'Ut quum manifestissimus sit sensus testatoris, verborum interpretatio nusquam tantum valeat, ut melior sensu existat' ('when the testator's intention is entirely manifest, verbal interpretation should never prevail over the sense'). This is the classical principle that intent prevails over wording in wills.

Following it is a bibliography on the compulsory portion (Pflichtteil) and disinheritance:
- Glück, Ausführliche Erläuterung der Pandecten, vol. VI § 543 and vol. VII §§ 547–561.
- G. Müller, Die Lehre vom Pflichttheile, 2 parts (Th. I Amberg u. Sulzbach 1801; Th. II Nürnberg u. Sulzbach 1806).
- Fr. Chr. Boock, Systematische Entwicklung der Lehre von der Enterbung, Schleswig 1799 (449 pp.).
- Valett, Das Recht der nothwendigen testamentarischen Berücksichtigung gewisser Verwandten, Göttingen 1826.

This presumably reflects Gauss's private concerns about wills and family inheritance. No mathematics serves any problem here. The mathematical content of the neighbouring folio (the next page, on circular-aperture diffraction) is unrelated to this page.
errors: The heading reads 'Dig.' (or similar), but the cited law 'l. 3 C. de lib. praet.' and the quoted text belong to the Codex Iustinianus (C. 6.28.3), not the Digest. This is either a minor slip by Gauss or a misreading of an abbreviation.

deep.surprise_reason: Purely personal and administrative notes: bond numbers and Roman/German inheritance-law references. There is no mathematical content.
transcription_corrections: 'Erl. des Pandects' should read 'Erl. der Pandecten' (Glück, Ausführliche Erläuterung der Pandecten).
'Dig. l 3 C. de lib. praet': the source is Codex 6.28.3 (de liberis praeteritis vel exheredatis); the leading abbreviation may be misread.
'sensus existat' in some readings should be 'sensu existat' (as the image shows).
'Valett' is probably J. Valett; 'Gött 1826' means Göttingen 1826.
